correctness.rationale: For fixed ell>0 and 0<alpha=s-1<1, renewal age A_t/t tends to Beta(1-alpha,alpha) via the regularly varying lattice renewal mass and survival tail; both endpoints are tight by the displayed power bounds. Spectral diagonalization of the specified three-state Grover coin and shift gives two dispersive branches plus a flat band; the reset coin chi_perp is orthogonal to the flat-band eigenspace at every momentum. An independent numerical projector check over 4 ell values and 31 momenta gave squared overlaps below 5e-31, corroborating but not proving the algebraic orthogonality. The pushforward of arcsine momentum under group velocity gives Konno density b/[pi(1-v^2)sqrt(a^2-v^2)] without an atom. Renewal mixing yields independent product Y=UV; Mellin/beta integrations give central x^(-alpha), front (a-x)^(alpha-1/2), positive constants and sharp transition at s=3/2. Beta E(U^2) times Konno E(V^2) reproduces the independently published second moment; tests of finitely many parameters do not establish general convergence.
residual_risks: Only ell>0 and 1<s<2 complete coin resets to chi_perp; one-time weak distribution, no endpoint exponents, atom-active initial coin, or pointwise lattice local limit.

originality.rationale: Das (2026) studies the identical weighted three-state walk and reset mechanism, flat-band-dark state, renewal weights, fixed-position limits, and power-law-restart second moments. Classical Dynkin–Lamperti ages and three-state Konno velocities are prior results; these ingredients do not by themselves explicitly state the beta*Konno weak spatial law, its full density, sharp central/front amplitudes and s=3/2 front transition. Classical ballistic Lévy walks accumulate flights rather than restarting from origin, so a Lévy-walk law cannot simply be substituted.
